answer: A concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with slow growth: each agent must lock a modest bond before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers prove it shares keys or coordinates with clones. Like an opal forming layer by layer, trust accrues only over time, so a grove of fresh identities planted overnight carries no weight. An ivory-tower shortcut — buying reputation wholesale — fails because bonds are per-identity, non-transferable, and forfeited on detection, making mass fabrication cost more than it can ever earn.
